title: ILLUMINE - Exploiting the Dark Proteome to fight cancer
text: Cells produce a previously under-appreciated class of non-standard proteins collectively termed the dark proteome that are not encoded by known open reading frames or explained by DNA mutations. The biological origins, regulation and functional role of the dark proteome in normal tissues and cancer remains largely unknown. This challenge aims to uncover the mechanisms that give rise to dark proteome products and to define their connection to the oncogenic state. Team ILLUMINE led by Reuven Agami (Netherlands Cancer Institute) brings together interdisciplinary researchers with expertise in cancer biology, proteomics, genomics, chemistry, technology development and clinical translation. The program will address four central questions: who the dark proteome players are, whether and how they are (dys)regulated in cancer, how they function, and how they can be therapeutically exploited. In addressing these questions, ILLUMINE will address major gaps in knowledge. Aim 1 will create a comprehensive map of dark proteome entities across several major cancer types and dissect potential stress-related mechanisms for their production. Aim 2 will codify a bench-to-bedside pre-clinical therapeutic development pipeline for immunotherapies from the dark proteome. Aim 3 will profile cell-based mechanisms of individual dark proteins in cancer biology, focusing on cell autonomous and non-cell autonomous mechanisms. Aim 4 will explore non-immunotherapy opportunities for targeting the dark proteome. Capitalizing on its unique expertise the team plans to use and combine cutting-edge experimental approaches to uncover hidden layers of cancer cell biology. ILLUMINE aims to ultimately identify new tumor biology and treatment paradigms for patients based on the dark proteome.

title: Mapping cell type specific isoform diversity in the human brain: dissecting mechanisms of alternative splicing in ASD
text:
Despite mounting genomic and transcriptomic evidence linking alternative splicing to autism spectrum disorder
(ASD), the underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. This project employs single nucleus long-read
sequencing to identify, quantify, and localize full-length isoforms into cell populations of the postnatal prefrontal
cortex, in individuals with and without a diagnosis of idiopathic ASD. Gaining insight into how brain-expressed
isoforms contribute to cell types, interact in biological pathways, and are dysregulated in the context of ASD, will
further our mechanistic understanding of brain function.

title: Molecular mechanisms of compound microtubule structure and function
text:
The centrosome-cilium complex is present in almost all cell types of the human body and is involved in cell
division, signaling, and motility. Defects in the structure or function of the complex are linked to a variety of human
diseases, including cancer, microcephaly, and ciliopathies. Our research will identify the mechanisms by which
the centrosome-cilium complex is built and regulated, contributing to our knowledge about disease progression
and potentially leading to the development of new therapies.

title: Injectable Hybrid SMART Spheroids to Enhance Stem Cell Therapy for CNS Injuries
text:
Our proposed studies are relevant to public health, as developing an injectable, biocompatible, and
biodegradable method to form therapeutic 3D spheroids to promote stem cell therapy will facilitate CNS repair
and modulate neuroinhibitory microenvironments after CNS injury. Therefore, the proposed research is relevant
to the part of NIH’s mission that relates to treating human illness and disability by investigating how innovative
technology can safely translate to clinics.

title: Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems (ENDS) Use and Access in Florida's Tobacco Regulatory Environment
text:
The recent vaping-related acute lung injuries and deaths as well as the first animal studies linking vaping to
cancer have highlighted the need to respond to e-cigarette use among youth. This study will assess the
relationship between e-cigarette retailer access and youth e-cigarette use, access, and exposure to marketing
in Florida, explore where, how, why, and from whom youth access e-cigarettes, and whether combined tobacco
regulations will reduce youth e-cigarette use and marketing exposure. It will also lay the groundwork for a tobacco
regulation-oriented research program that blends multiple methods of policy analysis to guide the translation of
disparities-focused research to evidence-based policy.

title: Them1 Inhibitors for the Management of Non Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because the early-stage preclinical validation of
therapeutic leads that target novel pathways of energy homeostasis and nutrient metabolism offers
promise for the management of obesity-related disorders. The proposed studies are relevant to the
mission of the NIDDK because they are expected to identify new lead compounds for the treatment of
non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

title: The Contribution of Age-Related Tauopathies to Alzheimer's Disease
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it will establish the contribution of the age-related
tauopathies, including chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), primary age-related tauopathy (PART),
progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), argyrophilic grain disease (AGD) and aging-related tau astrogliopathy
(ARTAG) to late life cognitive decline and neuropsychiatric symptoms. This project is relevant to NIA’s mission
of improving the health and well-being of older people because it will increase the accuracy of neuropathological
diagnosis in mild cognitive impairment and dementia, and will facilitate future research on the diagnosis,
treatment, and prevention of Alzheimer’s Disease and related disorders.

title: Control of retinal cell fate specification by the miR9-2 disease gene locus
text:
The nervous system is composed of cell classes of varied form, function, and genetic profile, yet often these
cells originate from the same population of multipotent progenitors. Here, I propose to elucidate the genetic
networks regulated by the microRNA, miR9-2 and its distal enhancer, using an in vivo miR9-2 knockout mouse
model which has been found to have retinal structure perturbations. This project will fill a gap in our knowledge
regarding the specific role of miR9-2 in cell types of the developing retina, its function as a genetic regulator, and
its potential contribution to disease.

title: Coordinating center for collaborative marmoset research
text:
The common marmoset (Callithrix jacchhus) has emerged as a critically important biomedical animal model.
Increased demand for marmosets in scientific research has been most acute in neuroscience, where the need
to study cognition, behavior, and mental illness in primate models with new genomic editing and gene targeting
methodologies has surged. This project will continue the operation of a national marmoset coordinating center,
that integrates genomic and demographic data on US marmoset populations, which together provide information
and access to animals for scientists in the broader neuroscience community.

title: The UCSC Genome Browser
text:
The UCSC Genome Browser (https://genome.ucsc.edu) brings together many sources of information to help
researchers and doctors understand the function of genes and other regions of the human genome. The
Browser helps researchers intelligently design therapies for a broad range of diseases. For diseases caused
by genetic variation, it helps doctors understand which variations cause which diseases.

title: Peptidoglycan modification activating NOD2 in N. gonorrhoeae infections
text:
The organism that causes gonorrhea elicits an immune response that is damaging to human tissue, causing
painful inflammation in gonorrhea and killing the ciliated cells of the oviduct during pelvic inflammatory disease.
These studies will determine mechanisms involved in the tissue damage and the mechanisms the bacteria use
to create the harmful cell wall fragments that elicit the response.

title: Development of a highly-multiplexed CRISPR-based TB drug susceptibility test
text:
Drug-resistant tuberculosis is a major global cause of morbidity and mortality with the need for rapid, accurate
drug susceptibility tests that can be performed outside of centralized labs. We will develop a highly-multiplexed
CRISPR TB drug susceptibility test to achieve comprehensive, accurate, and adaptable drug susceptibility
results, while integrating simplified workflows to enable deployment in settings closer to the patient.

title: Development and Validation of a Deep Learning system to estimate Interstitial Fibrosis from a kidney ultrasonography image
text:
Interstitial fibrosis a strong predictor of future decline in kidney function and development of kidney
failure is not readily available in most patients with kidney disease because: a) A kidney biopsy
which is rarely performed is needed to estimate interstitial fibrosis and b) A non-invasive test to
estimate interstitial fibrosis is not available. Kidney ultrasonography is a routine non-invasive test
in assessment of kidney disease and the current study will utilize artificial intelligence techniques
to develop a model to estimate interstitial fibrosis from a kidney ultrasonography image. The
proposed research is relevant to NIH mission because developing a non-invasive test to
estimate interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy will lead to better prediction of future decline in
kidney function and monitoring of treatment in all patients with kidney disease.

title: Illumina NovaSeq X Sequencing System
text:
Acquisition of the requested Illumina NovaSeq X Sequencing System will immediately enhance multiple NIH-
funded research efforts of 15 Major Users and 21 Other Users in 18 different departments or institutes at The
University of Texas Health at San Antonio and surrounding South Texas region. These investigators are engaged
in basic, translational and clinical research, and provide educational programs for a wide range of medical and
translational sciences. The high-throughput sequencing capabilities of the NovaSeq X will be critically important
to advancing these efforts and will play a central role in ensuring the long-term success of their research
programs.

title: Serotonergic Modulation of Auditory Cortical Circuits
text:
Serotonergic signaling modulates cortical plasticity, but the cellular and circuit-level mechanisms by which this
occurs remain to be elucidated. The proposed research will identify the cellular and synaptic targets of serotonin
in the auditory cortex and determine how serotonin modulates auditory cortical network activity. Findings from
this proposal may be used to inform the development of targeted pharmacological strategies to facilitate plasticity
and recover auditory function following hearing loss.

title: The Administrative Core
text: The Columbia University Digestive and Liver Disease Research Center seeks to combine innovative research concepts in its Biomedical Cores with outstanding clinical expertise, a large collection of biospecimens and a strong base of productive investigators to understand the causes and develop new treatment approaches for diseases of the digestive tract and liver, that are a major cause of morbidity and mortality.

title: Enhance UCSC Xena: extend interactive visualization to ultra-large-scale multi-omics data and integrate with analysis resources
text:
Our proposal will build the next generation of UCSC Xena to support interactive online visualization and
analysis of very large-scale, multi-omics single-cell and bulk tumor data, and integrate these high-performance
visualizations with NCI Cloud Resources. These enhancements will make comprehensive cancer genomics
reference datasets, including maps of all human cells and cellular mappings of cancers, more accessible to a
larger group of biomedical researchers. Our proposed work will also help individual researchers to securely
view their own data and analysis results from a cloud-based research environment.

title: Integrative metagenomics & metatranscriptomics features of enterohepatic recirculation in kidney transplant recipients
text:
Integrative metagenomics & metatranscriptomics features of enterohepatic recirculation in
kidney transplant recipients
DR. GUILLAUME ONYEAGHALA
UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS MEDICAL BRANCH
MAY 28, 2025
CENTER FOR SCIENTIFIC REVIEW
K01 MENTORED SCIENTIST CAREER DEVELOPMENT AWARD APPLICATION
(PA-24-176) Project Narrative
The administration of the major immunosuppressant mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) in kidney transplant
recipients (KTRs) requires drug monitoring of Mycophenolic acid (MPA), the active metabolite, as low
MPA exposure has been associated with acute allograft rejection in KTRs. MPA also undergoes
enterohepatic recirculation (EHR), which involves the reabsorption of MPA metabolites by the intestines
after biliary excretion, due to gastrointestinal bacteria expressing ßeta-Glucuronidase (ßGUS) enzymes.
Since a 12-hour MPA AUC to monitor MPA dose is not clinically feasible in the outpatient setting, In this
mentored research training proposal, we will apply advanced statistical and machine learning techniques
to the measurement of ßGUS proteomics and microbial metabolites, including trimethylamine N-oxide
(TAMO), indoxyl sulfate, and p-cresyl sulfate to determine their association with MPA pharmacokinetics
and allograft survival as potential non-invasive biomarkers of MPA variability.

title: Cancer Education and Research Program (CERP)
text:
In Arkansas, a disproportionate number of people in non-metropolitan areas are poor, have limited access to
healthcare and suffer from increased cancer morbidity and mortality. Educating and engaging high school
students in biomedical and cancer research improves access and reduces cancer burden and mortality.

title: The Role of Cell-Specific PD-L1 in cardiac pathophysiology post Ischemic Injury and Cancer
text:
Immunotherapy, particularly PD-1/PD-L1 blockers, is a highly effective cancer treatment, but it
carries the risk of rare but potentially fatal cardiotoxicities. The limited understanding of these
cardiotoxicities underscores the need for novel strategies to manage them, presenting significant
public health implications. The proposed work is of high significance as it addresses challenging
cardiac problems in immunotherapy (PD-L1-based) cancer patients lacking specific treatments.
